h: Planning a big day of splashing
p: With so many rides and attractions, it pays to have a rough plan. Start on the smaller slides and gentler features to warm up, then work up to the bigger thrills when everyone's settled in. If you've got a mix of ages in your group, split up for a bit and agree a meeting point, so the teens can tackle the big rides while younger ones play in the shallower areas.

Pack swimwear, towels, flip-flops and a change of warm clothes for afterwards. A bottle of water is a good idea, as swimming and climbing steps is thirsty work, and goggles help anyone who hates splashes in the eyes. Lockers are handy for keeping valuables safe, so grab one early.
How long to allow? Most families will want to make a good few hours of it, with a break for food. If you're adding mini golf or the mini village, plan for a full day out.
Waterworld sits on Festival Park in Hanley, part of the city's regenerated former steelworks land, so it's easy to reach and there are plenty of food options nearby.

Stoke-on-Trent's pottery heritage is worth exploring while you're here. The Gladstone Pottery Museum in Longton gives a real feel for life in the old potbanks, with bottle kilns you can walk into. The Emma Bridgewater factory in Hanley offers tours and the chance to decorate your own pottery, while the World of Wedgwood at Barlaston has a museum and factory tours.
For a calmer day afterwards, the Trentham Estate has gardens, lakeside walks and Trentham Monkey Forest, where Barbary macaques roam free in the woods.
